personas.name: urgent-suspected-angina-chest-pain-treadmill-complete
personas.description: Well-formed GP referral: suspected stable angina with chest pain, exercise treadmill ECG requested (first-line), patient able to exercise, no contraindications, every completeness field present. Chest pain plus a suspected-angina indication auto-escalates the rapid-access chest-pain pathway to urgent regardless of the routine urgency requested — expect usually-appropriate + ok + urgent + accept.

request.clinicalQuestion: Intermittent exertional chest tightness over 2 months, low-intermediate pre-test probability of CAD — assess for inducible ischaemia.
request.relevantHistory: No previous cardiac history. Hypertension well controlled on amlodipine.

symptoms.restingEcgFindings: Normal sinus rhythm, no ST-T changes.

triage.notes: Patient mobile and keen to exercise; no orthopaedic limitations.

firedRules.description: Requested exercise-treadmill-ecg is a recommended test for "suspected-angina".

personas.name: exercise-tolerance-treadmill-unable-to-exercise-redirect
personas.description: Exercise tolerance assessment ahead of a pulmonary rehabilitation programme: exercise treadmill ECG is the only listed ideal test for exercise-tolerance, so appropriateness scores well, but severe osteoarthritis means the patient cannot exercise on a treadmill — the exercise-safety rule redirects to a pharmacological/imaging alternative regardless of how appropriate the test choice was on paper — expect usually-appropriate + caution + routine + redirect.

request.clinicalQuestion: Formal exercise tolerance assessment ahead of pulmonary rehabilitation referral.
request.relevantHistory: Severe bilateral knee osteoarthritis, awaiting joint replacement. Uses a walking frame.

triage.notes: Patient cannot mobilise on a treadmill; consider pharmacological stress alternative.

expected.recommendationLabel: Redirect to a more suitable test

personas.name: emergency-recent-acs-contraindicated-incomplete
personas.description: Chest pain referral phoned through from the emergency department: exercise treadmill ECG would be first-line for suspected angina, but the patient had an NSTEMI four days ago — recent acute coronary syndrome is an absolute contraindication to stress testing until stabilised, and also forces emergency same-day cardiology review, overriding the routine-looking test request; several administrative fields are not yet captured — expect usually-appropriate + contraindicated + emergency + reject, completeness below 100.

request.relevantHistory: NSTEMI 4 days ago, treated with PCI to the right coronary artery. New exertional chest discomfort since discharge.

symptoms.restingEcgFindings: Q waves inferior leads, unchanged from post-PCI ECG.

triage.notes: Phoned through from ED; cardiology on-call already aware and reviewing.
